description: My go-to set of packages for any article or report: fonts, margins, maths, tables, figures, links.
name: Everyday preamble
notes: Order: everything else first, then `hyperref`, then `cleveref` last.
`microtype` improves spacing and line breaks for free. Always include it.
Download the `.sty` and `\usepackage{everyday-preamble}` to keep every document consistent.
With `T1` fontenc, accented characters and `<`/`>` in text come out right.

description: Shortcuts I use constantly: number sets, auto-sizing |abs| and ‖norm‖, argmin, expectation, upright d.
name: Maths shortcuts & operators
notes: `\DeclarePairedDelimiter` gives `\abs{x}` (fixed size) and `\abs*{x}` (grows to fit, like `\left|...\right|`).
`\DeclareMathOperator*` (starred) puts subscripts **under** the operator in display maths, as with argmin.
`\dd` gives an upright d with correct spacing: `\int f(x) \dd x`.
If a name clashes (e.g. another package defines `\C`), rename it here once.

description: Restyle `\section` and `\subsection`: a coloured heading with a thin rule underneath.
name: Coloured section headings
notes: `\titleformat{cmd}{format}{label}{sep}{before-code}[after-code]`. The rule goes in the optional last argument.
`\titlespacing*{\section}{left}{before}{after}`. The `*` removes the indent of the paragraph that follows.
Change `headingblue` once and every heading follows.

description: A numbered, captioned algorithm float with Require/Ensure, a loop, a condition and a return.
name: Algorithm pseudocode
notes: `[1]` after `algorithmic` numbers every line. Use `[0]` for none.
Keywords end with an explicit `\EndFor`, `\EndIf`, `\EndWhile` (algpseudocode style).
Use `\gets` for assignment (←). It reads better than `=`.
Rename Require/Ensure to Input/Output: `\renewcommand{\algorithmicrequire}{\textbf{Input:}}`.

description: `align` for several equations lined up on `=`, and `split` for one long equation with a single number.
name: Aligned & multi-line equations
notes: `&` marks the alignment point and `\\` ends a line. Use `align*` for no numbers at all.
`\nonumber` (or `\notag`) drops the number on a single line.
Reference with `\eqref{...}`, which adds the parentheses for you.
Never use `eqnarray`. Its spacing around `=` is wrong. Use `align`.

description: A clean, publication-style table: no vertical lines, proper rule spacing, caption above.
name: Booktabs table
notes: No vertical lines. booktabs rules look wrong with `|` columns.
`@{}` at both ends removes the outer padding so the rules line up with the text.
Put the `\caption` **above** a table and **below** a figure (the usual convention).
`\label` must come *after* `\caption`, otherwise `\ref` points at the section number.

description: Reusable coloured note and warning boxes with titles. They break across pages.
name: Callout boxes (tcolorbox)
notes: Define the box once with `\newtcolorbox` and the optional title argument `[1][Note]` sets a default.
`breakable` lets long boxes split across pages, and it needs `\tcbuselibrary{breakable}`.
Colours mix like `blue!55!black` (55% blue, 45% black). Keep backgrounds very light (`!4!white`).

description: Syntax-highlighted source code with line numbers, a light background and a caption.
name: Code listing with syntax colours
notes: `\lstset{style=mystyle}` applies the style everywhere. Override per listing with `[language=C, ...]`.
listings doesn't handle UTF-8 (é, ü, →) in code out of the box. Add `literate={é}{{\'e}}1` or switch to `minted`.
`minted` has nicer highlighting (Pygments) but needs `-shell-escape`. listings works everywhere, Overleaf included.
Include a file directly: `\lstinputlisting[language=Python]{script.py}`.

description: `\cref` writes "Figure 1", "Equation (2)", "Section 1" for you, as clickable links.
name: Smart cross-references (cleveref)
notes: Load order matters: `xcolor` before `hyperref` (for colour mixes like `blue!60!black`), `hyperref` near the end, `cleveref` **after** it.
`\cref{a,b}` handles lists ("Figures 1 and 2"). Use `\Cref` at the start of a sentence.
`[capitalise, noabbrev]` gives "Figure 1" instead of "fig. 1".
Labels: use prefixes like `fig:`, `tab:`, `eq:`, `sec:` so you can tell them apart.

description: Compact bullets, (a)/(b) labels, "Step 1:" labels and inline lists, all with enumitem.
name: Custom lists (enumitem)
notes: `noitemsep` removes the gap between items. `nosep` removes every gap, top and bottom included.
Label counters: `\arabic*` 1, `\alph*` a, `\Alph*` A, `\roman*` i, `\Roman*` I.
Inline lists need the `[inline]` package option and the starred environments (`enumerate*`).
Set it globally: `\setlist[itemize]{noitemsep}`.

description: The matrix environments, with (), [] and || delimiters, dots, and an augmented matrix.
name: Matrices & determinants
notes: `pmatrix` gives ( ), `bmatrix` [ ], `Bmatrix` { }, `vmatrix` | | (determinant), `Vmatrix` ‖ ‖.
Dots: `\cdots` (horizontal), `\vdots`, `\ddots`.
Augmented matrix: an `array` with `|` in the column spec, wrapped in `\left[ ... \right]`.
Inline in text: `$\left(\begin{smallmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{smallmatrix}\right)$`.

description: Cells spanning several rows or columns, with a partial rule under a grouped header.
name: Merged cells (multirow / multicolumn)
notes: `\multicolumn{n}{c}{text}` spans *n* columns. It's built in, no package needed.
`\multirow{n}{*}{text}` spans *n* rows. Leave the cells below it empty.
`\cmidrule(l){3-4}` draws a rule under columns 3–4; `(l)`/`(r)` trim its ends so neighbouring rules don't touch.

description: A line chart drawn natively in LaTeX: two data series and a function, with a grid and legend.
name: Line chart (pgfplots)
notes: Always set `\pgfplotsset{compat=...}` or you'll get old, ugly defaults and a warning.
Plot a CSV directly: `\addplot table [x=epoch, y=loss, col sep=comma] {data.csv};`
Fonts match your document automatically, which a matplotlib PNG never does.
Lots of points making it slow? Export from matplotlib with `tikzplotlib`, or use `external` to cache.

description: Piecewise definitions with a left brace and conditions, using `cases`.
name: Piecewise functions (cases)
notes: Use `\text{if } ...` for words inside maths so they get normal spacing and an upright font.
Want full-size fractions in the cases? Load `mathtools` and use `dcases` instead.

description: Two images next to each other, each with its own (a)/(b) caption, plus a shared caption.
name: Side-by-side figures (subcaption)
notes: `example-image-a` / `-b` come with the `mwe` package. Replace them with your own file names (no extension needed).
Keep the widths summing to just under 1 (`0.48 + 0.48`) and put `\hfill` between them.
`[b]` aligns the subfigures on their bottom edge, which matters when the images have different heights.
Three across? Use `0.32\textwidth` each.

description: Numbers aligned on the decimal point with the `S` column, plus consistent units in text.
name: Decimal-aligned numbers & units (siunitx)
notes: `table-format=2.3` means 2 integer digits and 3 decimals. It reserves the right width so the column is centred.
Wrap non-numeric header cells in braces `{...}` or siunitx tries to parse them as numbers.
In text: `\qty{9.81}{\metre\per\second\squared}`, `\num{6.022e23}`, `\unit{\kilo\gram}` (siunitx v3 names).

description: A table stretched to `\textwidth` where the `X` column wraps long text automatically.
name: Full-width table with wrapping text
notes: `X` columns share whatever width is left after the other columns.
`>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X` gives ragged-right text, which reads better than justified text in narrow cells.
Don't use `\verb` inside `tabularx`. It reads the whole body as an argument, so `\verb` breaks.

description: Numbered theorem, lemma and definition environments sharing one counter, plus `proof` with a QED box.
name: Theorems, definitions & proofs
notes: `[theorem]` in `\newtheorem{lemma}[theorem]{Lemma}` makes lemmas share the theorem counter (Theorem 1.1, Lemma 1.2, …).
`[section]` on the first one resets numbering every section. Drop it for 1, 2, 3, ….
The three styles: `plain` (italic body, for results), `definition` (upright), `remark` (lighter heading).
`\newtheorem*` (with a star) is unnumbered.

description: A complete short article: title, abstract, sections, an equation, a table and references.
name: Article
notes: Bibliography uses `thebibliography` so it compiles anywhere. Switch to BibTeX/biblatex once you have more than a handful of references.
Compile twice (or use latexmk) so the references and `\cref`s resolve.

description: A 16:9 Beamer talk: title slide, outline, step-by-step bullets, a two-column slide and a closing slide.
name: Slides (Beamer)
notes: `aspectratio=169` for modern screens. Remove it for 4:3.
`\item<2->` reveals an item from the 2nd click onwards. `\pause` is the quick alternative.
Navigation symbols are hidden because nobody uses them.
Print handouts without the overlays: `\documentclass[handout]{beamer}`.

description: Problem-set layout: header with course and name, boxed numbered problems, and solutions ending in ∎.
name: Homework / problem set
notes: `problem` takes an optional label: `\begin{problem}[10 points]`.
`solution` is amsthm's `proof` renamed, so you get the QED box for free.
Edit the course code and your name in the `\lhead` / `\rhead` lines once.

description: A university lab report: full title page, running header, and Aim → Theory → Method → Results → Discussion.
name: Lab report
notes: `titlepage` gives an unnumbered page of its own. `\vfill` pushes the details to the bottom.
Header/footer are set with `fancyhdr`. `\fancyhf{}` clears the defaults first.
Use `siunitx` for every measured value so units and uncertainties stay consistent.
